title: The ocean has a noise problem
text: The sea has grown {{1}} noisier since the 1950s, and for whales — {{2}} world is built on sound — the difference matters more than any of us can easily imagine. Ship engines, {{3}} rumble at exactly the frequencies whales use to talk, force them {{4}} shout over the din, and shy species simply fall silent. Quieter propellers already exist, {{5}}, and retro-fitting them costs shipowners remarkably {{6}}. In 2020, {{7}} shipping slowed during the pandemic, researchers measured an immediate drop in ocean noise and, in some regions, whales relaxed back into their old calls almost overnight. The quietest year in a century became an unplanned experiment {{8}} one conclusion: the noise was never unavoidable — it was merely nobody's job to notice.

gaps.explanation: Intensifier before the comparative: much noisier.

gaps.hint: relative: whales — ___ world is built on sound
gaps.explanation: 'Whose' links the whales to their world.

gaps.hint: relative: engines, ___ rumble at whale frequencies
gaps.explanation: Non-defining relative after the pair of commas.
'Force someone to do' — the infinitive follows the object.

gaps.hint: linker: propellers exist, ___, and fitting costs

gaps.explanation: Uncountable cost, small amount: remarkably little.
Non-defining time clause after the year.
'An experiment with one conclusion' — the fixed phrase.
